title: Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review of the 2025 Budget Statement and Economic Policy of the Government of Ghana (theme: Resetting the Economy for the Ghana We Want)
presented_by: Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson (MP), Minister for Finance
source_note: 2025-Mid-Year-Fiscal-Policy-Review.pdf (95 pages). Page numbers are PDF pages; printed page numbers are PDF page minus 3.
headline_summary: Government kept all 2025 macroeconomic targets and the GH¢293.1bn appropriation unchanged (real GDP growth of at least 4.0%, end-year inflation 11.9%, primary surplus 1.5% of GDP, reserves of at least 3 months of imports), pointing to a strong first half: Q1 growth of 5.3%, inflation down from 23.8% to 13.7%, the cedi up 42.6% against the US dollar, reserves at 4.8 months of imports and public debt down from 61.8% to 43.8% of GDP. The fiscal framework was nonetheless revised to absorb the GH¢1-per-litre Energy Sector Shortfall and Debt Repayment Levy: revenue and grants rise to GH¢229.9bn (16.4% of GDP), interest costs fall by GH¢4.3bn on lower T-bill rates, and energy-sector payments rise by GH¢2.9bn. As a result the overall deficit targets improve from 3.1% to 2.8% of GDP (commitment) and from 4.1% to 3.8% (cash), while H1 revenue was 3.2% below target and the Minister flagged customs shortfalls, marine gas oil smuggling and a GH¢1.3bn wage overrun as risks.

shortfalls_admitted.text: Petroleum receipts fell short of target by GH¢2.7bn (delayed oil CIT receipts, cedi appreciation)

Non-oil non-tax revenue GH¢8.0bn, 15.6% below the GH¢9.5bn target
Arrears clearance GH¢4.8bn against a GH¢7.5bn target
Project loan disbursements GH¢2.4bn vs GH¢8.3bn target due to slower execution and portfolio repurposing
Capital expenditure GH¢7,105.1m vs GH¢18,058.5m programmed for H1 (Figure 5 / Appendix 2A)
Wages and salaries exceeded the budget by GH¢1.3bn in H1 (late-2024 recruitment, ad hoc service-condition reviews)
MGO tax exemptions abused, with revenue losses estimated at nearly half a billion cedis

data_quality_notes: All pages are PDF page numbers; printed page = PDF page - 3. The PDF has 95 pages; the text extract has an empty 96th marker.

The review's '2025 Budget' column differs from the budget-statement figures in 2025.json: revenue & grants 227,080.4 vs 224,933.6 and total expenditure 270,924.1 vs 268,777.3 (both +2,146.8, via non-tax revenue 26,548.0 vs 24,401.2); compensation 76,203.2 vs 76,640.1; goods & services 6,671.1 vs 6,971.1; grants to other govt units 54,566.6 vs 54,467.5; other expenditure 33,079.2 (includes a GoldBod line of 4,547.7) vs 30,044.6; capex 32,661.6 vs 32,991.6; appropriation 293,118.0 vs 290,971.2. Revenue % of GDP is 16.2 here vs 16.1 in 2025.json. 'original' columns use the review's own figures; 2025.json values are in baseline_2025json_ghs_m.
Table 2 (p65) total expenditure 283,992 (20.3%) to 282,564 (20.2%) equals Appendix 3A expenditure plus arrears clearance (270,924.1 + 13,067.6). The appendix basis is used in fiscal_revised.
The section heading on p64 reads 'Revision to the 2024 Fiscal Framework'; context shows it is the 2025 framework.
The p22 text gives the H1 goods & services target as 'GH¢3.2 million'; Appendix 2A shows GH¢3,158.5m (billion).
H1 overall commitment balance: -10,254.9 (Appendix 2A, p85) vs -10,339.6 (memorandum incl. discrepancy, p86).
H1 amortisation: -4,166.1 (Appendix 2A financing, p86) vs 7,036.4 (Appendix 2C, p88).
Net domestic issuance is given as GH¢8bn (p33) and GH¢8.4bn (p37).
Appendix 3B (p91) prints grants as 0.5% of GDP, which does not match GH¢2,674.6m / GH¢1,400,006m (0.2%, as on p87); revised_pct_gdp left null.
The p32 text says debt/GDP 'reduced by 18%'; this is 18 percentage points (61.8% to 43.8%).
GIR at end-Dec 2024: US$8.98bn (p13, p26) vs US$9.0bn (Box 1, p25). The 91-day T-bill is 14.73% (p13) or rounded to 14.7% (p18).

The monetary policy rate is not stated anywhere in the review. The benchmark crude price and full-year crude output are not restated or revised; only Jan–May 2025 production (15.32m barrels) is given. OCTP non-associated gas rate is 249.91 mmscf/d on p54 but 246.91 on p55.
Pages 25 (Box 1 on cedi appreciation) and 33 (Figure 7) are image-only; figures quoted from them were read visually. Page 40 is blank.
The ESLA amendment is cited as Act 1135 amended on 3 June 2025 (p44) and as Act 1141 (p64).

Commitment status convention: 'done' = completed per the review; 'on track' = progress reported with no admitted slippage (not a forecast that the full-year target will be hit); 'delayed' = behind H1 programme or a stated deadline, or rescheduled; 'not started' = the review says the action has yet to begin; 'not mentioned' = no progress reported (a page is given where the item is referenced without metrics).

Commitments 2025-24, 2025-25 and 2025-28 are marked 'not mentioned' because the narrative is silent, although appendix tables show related revenue lines (E-Levy H1 GH¢812.7m; GSL GH¢1,085.3m vs GH¢2,026.2m programme; refunds GH¢5,074.4m vs GH¢3,423.6m).
Commitment 2025-53 refers to Tema–Adome; the review reports the Tema–Mpakadan line (97.7km).
Text says total cash of GH¢114.5bn was paid from the Consolidated Fund Jan–Jun (p78), which differs from total expenditure of GH¢109.6bn (commitment) in Appendix 2A.
Amounts converted from GH¢ units in the appendices to GH¢ million, rounded to 1 decimal.
